notes: Distinct fictional probability, performance, filing, and corporate-action concepts 581–600. Source/rights and independent numerical review pending.

guides.title: Risk-of-ruin model limits
guides.concept: Risk-of-ruin is a model output driven by uncertain assumptions, not a survival guarantee.
guides.prerequisites: Understand probability, payoff distributions, dependence, drawdown, and fixed-risk assumptions.
guides.procedure: Declare model, sample, risk fraction, distribution, and dependence assumptions; stress adverse alternatives.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Equal +1R/−1R outcomes yield +0.10R expectancy at 55% wins but −0.04R at 48%.
guides.limit: Real outcomes can be dependent, fat-tailed, nonstationary, and worse than planned.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when the formula, assumptions, sample, or loss cap is unsupported.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Reporting a tiny ruin probability to many decimals hides input uncertainty. Correct with ranges and stress cases.
guides.selfCheck: Which changed assumption turns fictional expectancy negative?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: the fictional expectancy changes sign when the win assumption changes. This demonstrates model sensitivity, not guaranteed survival.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: With +1R/−1R outcomes and 45% wins, compute expected R and name two model failures.

guides.title: Expectancy from an outcome distribution
guides.concept: Trade expectancy is the probability-weighted mean of a defined outcome distribution.
guides.prerequisites: Understand probabilities, R-multiples, weighted averages, and sample uncertainty.
guides.procedure: List mutually exclusive outcomes, verify probabilities sum to one, multiply each probability by outcome, and sum.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 40% at +2R, 50% at −1R, and 10% at 0R gives 0.4×2−0.5=+0.3R.
guides.limit: Estimated probabilities and payoffs may change and do not predict the next trade.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when outcomes overlap, probabilities do not sum to one, or costs are inconsistent.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Averaging +2R and −1R without their frequencies overstates performance. Correct with probability weights.
guides.selfCheck: Why must outcome probabilities sum to one?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional weighted expectancy is +0.3R. It is conditional on the stated distribution.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 30% at +3R, 60% at −1R, 10% flat; compute expectancy and name one estimation risk.

guides.title: Win rate and sample size
guides.concept: A sample win rate is wins divided by eligible completed observations and carries sampling uncertainty.
guides.prerequisites: Understand eligible samples, completed trades, proportions, exclusions, and confidence uncertainty.
guides.procedure: Freeze eligibility rules, count wins and total completed cases, divide once, and report sample size beside the rate.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: 18 wins among 30 eligible completed cases produce 60%; three open cases are excluded.
guides.limit: Thirty observations do not establish a stable future probability.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when cases are cherry-picked, duplicated, open, or defined inconsistently.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Reporting 60% without n=30 hides uncertainty. Correct by showing numerator, denominator, and exclusions.
guides.selfCheck: Which observations belong in the denominator?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional rate is 18/30=60%, explicitly tied to its sample.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 22 wins from 40 eligible completed cases; compute rate and list one invalid exclusion.

guides.title: Profit factor denominator
guides.concept: Profit factor divides gross profits by the absolute value of gross losses under one cost convention.
guides.prerequisites: Understand gross profit, gross loss, absolute values, costs, and zero denominators.
guides.procedure: Sum positive results, sum absolute negative results, verify consistent net-or-gross treatment, then divide.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Gross profits $900 and gross losses −$600 produce profit factor 900/600=1.5.
guides.limit: Profit factor omits sequence, sample size, capital, and tail risk.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when losses equal zero or trades and costs use inconsistent definitions.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Dividing by signed −$600 reports −1.5. Correct with absolute gross loss.
guides.selfCheck: Why is the loss denominator an absolute amount?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional profit factor is 1.5; it is not a return percentage or guarantee.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Gross profits $1,240 and losses −$800; calculate factor and state one limitation.

guides.title: Maximum drawdown from an equity path
guides.concept: Maximum drawdown is the largest peak-to-later-trough decline in an ordered equity path.
guides.prerequisites: Understand chronological equity, running peaks, troughs, deposits, and withdrawals.
guides.procedure: Order observations, adjust external cash flows consistently, track each running peak, and calculate later declines.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Equity peaks at $12,000 then reaches $10,800; drawdown is $1,200 or 10% of that peak.
guides.limit: Observation frequency can miss intraperiod drawdowns.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when timestamps, cash flows, currency, or equity definition is inconsistent.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Measuring from starting equity instead of the running peak can miss the true decline. Correct with chronological peaks.
guides.selfCheck: Which earlier value anchors each drawdown?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional peak-to-trough decline is 10%; order matters.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Equity peaks at $25,000 then falls to $22,250; compute drawdown dollars and percent.

guides.title: Return with external cash flow
guides.concept: Deposits and withdrawals must be separated from investment performance.
guides.prerequisites: Understand beginning value, ending value, cash flows, timing, and return conventions.
guides.procedure: Declare a return method and cash-flow timing; never treat contributed capital as profit.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Account starts $10,000, receives $2,000 immediately, and ends $12,600; simple return on $12,000 invested is 5%.
guides.limit: Midperiod cash flows require time-weighted or money-weighted methods rather than this immediate-flow simplification.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when cash-flow amount, direction, timing, or valuation times are missing.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling the $2,600 balance increase a 26% gain counts a deposit as performance. Correct by isolating cash flow.
guides.selfCheck: Which balance increase came from the owner rather than markets?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: after separating the immediate deposit, fictional gain is $600 on $12,000.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Start $8,000, immediate deposit $1,000, end $9,450; compute simplified return.

guides.title: Arithmetic versus geometric return
guides.concept: Arithmetic average describes mean period return, while geometric return preserves compounding across periods.
guides.prerequisites: Understand percentages, growth factors, products, and nonpositive wealth limits.
guides.procedure: For arithmetic mean add period returns and divide; for geometric mean multiply one-plus-return factors and take the appropriate root.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: +50% then −50% has arithmetic mean 0%, but $100 becomes $75 and geometric return is about −13.4% per period.
guides.limit: Neither average alone describes risk, path, or future return.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when periods differ, cash flows intervene, or return conventions mix.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling +50% and −50% break-even ignores the smaller base after loss. Correct with compounded wealth.
guides.selfCheck: Why does a zero arithmetic mean still lose capital here?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional growth factor is 1.5×0.5=0.75, not 1.0.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: +20% then −20% from $1,000; compute ending wealth and arithmetic mean.

guides.title: Volatility annualization assumption
guides.concept: Square-root-of-time annualization depends on interval, session count, and return-distribution assumptions.
guides.prerequisites: Understand standard deviation, daily returns, annual trading-day conventions, and serial dependence.
guides.procedure: State return type, sample convention, daily estimate, annualization factor, and why independence may fail.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Daily volatility 1.2% annualized with √252 is about 19.0% under the stated convention.
guides.limit: Volatility clustering, jumps, and changing regimes weaken square-root scaling.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when interval, sample, missing days, or annualization convention is undisclosed.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Multiplying 1.2% by 252 produces 302.4%. Correct by distinguishing volatility scaling from return addition.
guides.selfCheck: Which assumption supports square-root scaling?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional annualized estimate is about 19%, conditional on the convention.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Daily volatility 0.8%; estimate √252 annualized volatility and state one failure mode.

guides.title: Survivorship bias in a sample
guides.concept: A sample containing only securities still visible today can omit failures and overstate historical outcomes.
guides.prerequisites: Understand universe membership, delistings, mergers, selection dates, and point-in-time data.
guides.procedure: Freeze the eligible universe at each historical date and retain delisted or merged records with documented outcomes.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Ten stocks start; two delist after large losses. Measuring only eight survivors excludes 20% of the starting names.
guides.limit: Complete point-in-time constituent and delisting data may require licensed sources.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when historical membership or terminal outcomes cannot be reconstructed lawfully.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Backtesting today's winners across the past gives them knowledge of survival. Correct with point-in-time membership.
guides.selfCheck: Which missing records make the sample biased?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional survivor-only set drops two failed names and cannot represent the starting universe.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Fifteen names begin and three disappear; compute survivor share and explain the bias.

guides.title: Lookahead bias and filing availability
guides.concept: A filing value becomes eligible only when the filing was publicly available, not at the period-end date it describes.
guides.prerequisites: Understand reporting periods, filing timestamps, amendments, and decision cutoffs.
guides.procedure: Record period end and public filing time separately; use the earliest verified public version available before the decision.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Quarter ends March 31, filing appears May 8; an April 15 screen cannot use the filed value.
guides.limit: Vendor ingestion may lag the official public filing timestamp.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when publication time, form version, amendment status, or time zone is unknown.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Backdating May information to March creates impossible foresight. Correct with availability timestamps.
guides.selfCheck: Which date controls use in an April 15 decision?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional May 8 value is ineligible on April 15 despite its March period end.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Period ends June 30 and filing appears August 7; classify availability on July 20.

guides.title: Revenue growth with comparable periods
guides.concept: Revenue growth requires comparable periods, currencies, and continuing-business definitions.
guides.prerequisites: Understand income statements, fiscal periods, percentage change, restatements, and acquisitions.
guides.procedure: Verify period lengths and scope, subtract prior revenue from current, divide by prior revenue, and disclose structural changes.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Comparable quarterly revenue rises from $40m to $46m; growth=(46−40)/40=15%.
guides.limit: Acquisitions, currency translation, and recognition changes can reduce comparability.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when prior revenue is zero, periods differ, or restated figures are unresolved.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Comparing a 14-week quarter with 13 weeks as pure organic growth misstates evidence. Correct for comparability.
guides.selfCheck: Which denominator produces the fictional 15%?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional growth is 15% only under comparable scope and periods.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Comparable revenue rises from $25m to $28m; compute growth and name one comparability defect.

guides.title: Gross margin and consistent units
guides.concept: Gross margin divides revenue minus cost of revenue by revenue using the same period and units.
guides.prerequisites: Understand revenue, cost of revenue, percentages, units, and classification policies.
guides.procedure: Align period and units, compute gross profit, divide by nonzero revenue, and inspect classification changes.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Revenue $80m and cost of revenue $52m give gross profit $28m and margin 35%.
guides.limit: Gross margin excludes many operating, financing, and tax costs.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when revenue is zero, units differ, or cost classifications changed materially.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Dividing gross profit by cost produces 53.8%, not gross margin. Correct with revenue denominator.
guides.selfCheck: What is the correct gross-margin denominator?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional margin is 28/80=35%; it is not net profitability.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Revenue $50m and cost $32m; compute gross margin and one excluded expense class.

guides.title: Operating cash flow versus net income
guides.concept: Net income and operating cash flow measure different accounting effects and should be reconciled, not treated as interchangeable.
guides.prerequisites: Understand accrual accounting, noncash items, working capital, and cash-flow statements.
guides.procedure: Read both same-period figures, identify disclosed reconciliation items, and avoid labeling either alone as cash earnings.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Net income is $12m and operating cash flow $7m; the $5m difference requires reconciliation, not automatic fraud inference.
guides.limit: One period may reflect legitimate working-capital timing or noncash adjustments.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when periods, currencies, continuing operations, or cash-flow classification do not match.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling a difference proof of manipulation assigns motive without evidence. Correct by inspecting filed reconciliation.
guides.selfCheck: Why can the two measures differ legitimately?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional $5m gap is an observation requiring causes, not a verdict.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Net income $4m and operating cash flow $9m; calculate difference and list two possible reconciliation categories.

guides.title: Current ratio and classification
guides.concept: Current ratio divides current assets by current liabilities at one balance-sheet date.
guides.prerequisites: Understand balance sheets, current classification, ratios, seasonal timing, and nonzero denominators.
guides.procedure: Use same-date filed amounts, verify classification, divide current assets by nonzero current liabilities, and disclose seasonality.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Current assets $30m and current liabilities $20m give a current ratio of 1.5.
guides.limit: The ratio does not reveal asset quality, cash timing, or covenant compliance.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when dates differ, liabilities are zero, or classifications are not comparable.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling 1.5 proof of liquidity ignores receivable and inventory quality. Correct with component review.
guides.selfCheck: Which same-date amounts form the ratio?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional ratio is 30/20=1.5, with material qualitative limits.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Current assets $18m and liabilities $24m; compute ratio and name one quality question.

guides.title: Diluted EPS and share count
guides.concept: Diluted EPS uses the issuer's applicable diluted weighted-average shares, not simply ending shares outstanding.
guides.prerequisites: Understand net income available to common shareholders, weighted shares, dilution, and loss-period rules.
guides.procedure: Use filed numerator and diluted weighted-average denominator for the same period and inspect anti-dilution treatment.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: $10m available income divided by 5m diluted weighted-average shares gives $2.00 diluted EPS.
guides.limit: Potential shares and anti-dilutive treatment depend on accounting rules and period conditions.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when numerator, denominator, period, class, or restatement status differs.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Dividing by quarter-end shares can distort per-share results. Correct with the filed weighted-average denominator.
guides.selfCheck: Why is an ending share count not automatically valid?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional diluted EPS is $2 under matched filed inputs.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: $7.2m available income and 4.8m diluted weighted shares; compute EPS and state one caveat.

guides.title: Stock split and per-share comparability
guides.concept: A stock split changes share count and per-share price mechanically, so historical per-share comparisons need consistent adjustment.
guides.prerequisites: Understand split ratios, effective dates, raw versus adjusted values, and wealth invariance before costs.
guides.procedure: Verify official ratio and effective date, apply ratio consistently to shares and per-share values, and label raw or adjusted data.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Before a 3-for-1 split, 100 shares at $60 become 300 shares near $20; position value remains $6,000 before market movement.
guides.limit: Actual opening price can move and fractional-share handling may differ.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when ratio, effective date, security class, or adjustment state is missing.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Treating the raw drop from $60 to $20 as a 66.7% loss ignores tripled shares. Correct for the split.
guides.selfCheck: Which two quantities change inversely in the example?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional shares triple while theoretical per-share price divides by three.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 80 shares at $50 undergo 2-for-1 split; compute theoretical shares, price, and value.

guides.title: Cash dividend and ex-date interpretation
guides.concept: A cash dividend transfers value and can affect the ex-date price; raw price change alone is not total return.
guides.prerequisites: Understand declaration, record and ex-dates, dividend eligibility, taxes, and total return.
guides.procedure: Verify official dividend and ex-date, separate price return from cash distribution, and use a declared tax and reinvestment convention.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Price moves from $40 to $39.60 across a $0.50 dividend; raw price return is −1%, while pretax simple total return is +0.25%.
guides.limit: Market movement, taxes, currency, and reinvestment affect investor results.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when dividend amount, eligibility, prices, or corporate-action status is unverified.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling the 40-cent raw decline the entire loss omits the 50-cent distribution. Correct with total-return components.
guides.selfCheck: Which cash component changes the interpretation?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional total change is +$0.10 on $40, or +0.25%, before taxes and costs.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Price falls $25 to $24.70 across a $0.40 dividend; compute raw and pretax simple total return.

guides.title: Rights offering and dilution context
guides.concept: A rights offering changes financing and potential share count; a headline discount alone does not determine holder outcome.
guides.prerequisites: Understand subscription rights, record dates, exercise ratios, proceeds, dilution, and tradability.
guides.procedure: Read the official filing, identify eligible holders, ratio, price, dates, and potential shares; compare scenarios without assuming participation.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: One new share per four old shares could add 2.5m shares to 10m outstanding if fully exercised, a 25% increase.
guides.limit: Proceeds, participation, expenses, and use of funds affect economic consequences.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when terms, class, exercise status, or final participation is unknown.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling a 25% share increase an automatic 25% value loss ignores proceeds and market response. Correct with full terms.
guides.selfCheck: What does the fictional 25% measure and not measure?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional ratio describes potential share-count increase, not automatic price loss.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: One new share per five on 20m old shares; compute maximum new shares and percent increase.

guides.title: Reverse-split mechanics
guides.concept: A reverse split reduces share count and raises theoretical per-share price inversely without creating economic value by itself.
guides.prerequisites: Understand split ratios, fractional shares, effective dates, listings, and raw versus adjusted series.
guides.procedure: Verify official ratio and date, divide shares and multiply theoretical price by the ratio, then reconcile fractional treatment.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A 1-for-10 reverse split turns 1,000 shares near $0.80 into 100 shares near $8, preserving $800 before movement.
guides.limit: Rounding, cash in lieu, fees, and subsequent price movement can change actual value.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when ratio, eligible class, effective time, or fractional-share policy is absent.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Calling $0.80 to $8 a tenfold gain ignores the tenfold share reduction. Correct with position value.
guides.selfCheck: Why is the price increase not automatically a profit?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional share count and price move inversely; value is unchanged before other effects.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: 600 shares at $1.50 undergo 1-for-6 reverse split; compute theoretical shares, price, and value.

guides.title: Filing amendment and version control
guides.concept: An amended filing is a new dated source version and must not silently overwrite what was knowable earlier.
guides.prerequisites: Understand filing accession identifiers, amendments, timestamps, decision cutoffs, and audit trails.
guides.procedure: Store original and amended accession, public timestamps, changed fields, and which version was eligible for each decision.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Original filing May 1 reports 12 units; amendment May 10 reports 10. A May 5 decision must retain 12 as then-known.
guides.limit: An amendment may change only selected fields; full scope requires document comparison.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when accession, publication time, changed field, or decision cutoff is unverified.
guides.commonError: Live-trading mistake: Replacing May 1 data with May 10 data in a May 5 replay introduces lookahead. Correct with versioned evidence.
guides.selfCheck: Which value is eligible for a May 5 replay?
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: fictional May 5 evidence remains the original 12-unit value; later correction is separately recorded.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Original June 2 value 30, amendment June 8 value 27; classify evidence for June 5 and June 10 decisions.
